section_1.title: Prerequisite: The Wave Nature of Light
section_1.content: Briefly revisit superposition and path difference. Explain that coherent light (lasers) maintains a constant phase relationship, which is the foundational requirement for interference.
section_1.example: Visualizing two ripples in a pond intersecting to create fixed nodes and anti-nodes.

section_2.title: Diffraction: The Bending of Light
section_2.content: Define diffraction as the spreading of waves around obstacles. Use Huygens-Fresnel principle to explain how every point on a wavefront acts as a secondary source.
section_2.example: Animation showing a laser beam passing through a tiny slit, spreading into a characteristic 'sinc function' intensity pattern on a wall.

section_3.title: Holography: Recording the Interference Pattern
section_3.content: Explain that while standard photography captures only amplitude (brightness), holography records both amplitude and phase by interfering an object beam with a reference beam.
section_3.example: A 3D model of a 'Cyber-Owl' robot: showing the reference beam (direct light) and object beam (reflected light) meeting at the film plate to form complex interference fringes.

section_4.title: Reconstruction: The Diffraction Gate
section_4.content: Describe the hologram as a 'complex diffraction grating.' When illuminated by the reference beam, the interference fringes diffract light to recreate the original wavefronts, tricking the eye into seeing a 3D image.
section_4.example: An animation of a light beam hitting a 'holographic credit card sticker,' where the fringes act as a gate that bends light into the exact shape of the original 3D object.

section_5.title: Summary & Application
section_5.content: Summarize that a hologram is essentially a diffraction pattern stored on a medium. Discuss real-world uses in data storage and security.
section_5.example: Visualizing a futuristic HUD (Heads-Up Display) in a character's helmet that uses holographic diffraction to project navigation arrows onto the real-world view.

import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=20, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                # Shift right to give room for lecture text
                x = 1.5 + j * 0.8
                y = 2.2 - i * 0.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        center = (tl_pos + br_pos) / 2
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Holograms act like complex diffraction gratings.",
            "Reference beams hit fringes to recreate wavefronts.",
            "This reconstructs the original 3D optical field.",
            "The observer perceives depth through diffracted light.",
            "Diffraction gates recreate the object's original shape."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Reconstruction: The Diffraction Gate", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        hologram_plate = Rectangle(width=2, height=3, color=GRAY, fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(hologram_plate, "C3")
        
        beam = Line(start=[-2, 0, 0], end=self.grid["C3"], color=RED, stroke_width=4)
        
        diffracted_rays = VGroup(*[
            Line(start=self.grid["C3"], end=self.grid[pos], color=YELLOW) 
            for pos in ["B5", "C5", "D5"]
        ])
        
        cyber_owl = SVGMobject("assets/cyber_owl.svg" if False else None) # Placeholder logic
        # Since I don't have the real asset, creating a simple geometric proxy
        cyber_owl = VGroup(Circle(radius=0.3, color=BLUE), Triangle().scale(0.3).shift(UP*0.3))
        self.place_at_grid(cyber_owl, "C5")
        
        wavefront_label = Text("Reconstructed Wavefront", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(wavefront_label, "A3")
        wavefront_label.set_opacity(0)
        
        grating_label = Text("Complex Diffraction Grating", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(grating_label, "E3")
        grating_label.set_opacity(0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(hologram_plate))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(Create(beam))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF00FF")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(Create(diffracted_rays), FadeIn(cyber_owl))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#00FF00")
        grating_label.set_opacity(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        wavefront_label.set_opacity(1)
        
        self.wait(2)
